common_name: Watermelon Wine Itoh Peony (Single Raspberry-Pink Intersectional Peony)

planting.note: Plant bare-root divisions in fall 4-6 weeks before hard freeze, setting eyes no more than 1-2 in below the soil surface, in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun to light afternoon shade.

directions: Watermelon Wine is an Itoh (intersectional) hybrid bred by Roger Anderson, bearing huge single blooms of dark raspberry-pink with a deep wine-red flare at the base of each petal surrounding a boss of yellow stamens. Plant divisions with eyes shallow, just 1-2 in below grade, in rich, well-drained soil, since burying Itoh peonies too deep is the most common cause of poor flowering. The sturdy, woody-based stems need no staking and the plant blooms over an unusually long period for a peony, with light fragrance. Established plants are long-lived and tolerate more summer heat and a wider soil pH range than straight herbaceous lactiflora cultivars.

common_name: Takara Itoh Peony (Color-Changing Treasure Intersectional Peony)

planting.note: Plant bare-root divisions in fall 4-6 weeks before hard freeze, with eyes just 1-2 in below the soil surface, in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun.

directions: Takara, registered as 'Smith Opus 2', is an Itoh hybrid from breeder Donald R. Smith whose nearly 6-in blooms open pale yellow heavily flushed with lavender-pink, then fade over several days to a soft near-white with a dark burgundy flare at the center, so a single plant can show several color phases at once. Set divisions shallow in rich, well-drained soil in full sun, since Itoh peonies planted too deep often sulk and fail to bloom. Its strong, woody-based stems carry the large double flowers upright without staking and the foliage remains attractive through fall. Give it the same winter chill and fertile conditions favored by other intersectional peonies for best performance.

common_name: Yankee Doodle Dandy Itoh Peony (Semi-Double Pink-and-Cream Intersectional Peony)

planting.note: Plant bare-root divisions in fall 4-6 weeks before hard freeze, with eyes no more than 1-2 in below the soil surface, in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun.

directions: Yankee Doodle Dandy is an Itoh hybrid from breeder D.R. Smith, carrying large semi-double flowers of rich pink overlaid with cream tones around a prominent cluster of bright yellow stamens. As with other intersectional peonies, set divisions shallow in rich, well-drained soil, since deep planting is the main reason Itoh types fail to flower well. Sturdy, woody-based stems hold the blooms upright through spring rain without staking, and the compact clump keeps attractive foliage after bloom. It benefits from the same winter dormancy and occasional light feeding as other garden peonies.

common_name: Love Affair Itoh Peony (Semi-Double White Intersectional Peony)

planting.note: Plant bare-root divisions in fall 4-6 weeks before hard freeze, with eyes just 1-2 in below the soil surface, in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun to light afternoon shade.

directions: Love Affair is an Itoh hybrid bred by Don Hollingsworth, bearing midseason, semi-double white flowers with cupped petals that form a symmetrical bowl, typically one bloom per sturdy stem, on a compact, dark-green-leaved plant. Plant divisions shallow in fertile, well-drained soil, since burying the eyes too deep is the most frequent cause of poor flowering in intersectional peonies. The woody-based stems need no staking and hold the outfacing blooms well above the foliage, which stays clean and ornamental after bloom. Give it a cold winter dormancy and avoid soggy soil, as for other garden peonies.
